purpose: MAXIMALLY ADVERSARIAL entity-resolution stress test. The subject uses deliberate name-fragmentation (a real benami/laundering tradecraft) — his own name in many forms + similarly-named DISTINCT associates. The system must MERGE the subject's forms into one person AND keep distinct associates separate, resisting initial-collision and token-order-collision false merges.

GROUND_TRUTH_CAST.note: This is the answer key. Grade the report's entity resolution against this.

PERSON_A_SUBJECT.note: Uses variant name-forms as benami fragmentation. Should be identified as the single primary subject.

PERSON_B_associate1.why_confusable: Same tokens as the subject (Ramesh/Kumar) but REVERSED order and initial S (not R). This is the killer test — a naive matcher will wrongly merge B into A.

PERSON_C_associate2.why_confusable: Shares only the token 'Ramesh' with the subject.

PERSON_D_associate3.why_confusable: Shares only the token 'Kumar' with the subject.

PERSON_E_associate4.why_confusable: Shares only the INITIAL 'R.' with the subject — tests initial-collision false merge.

MERGE_test.check: Are all 5 forms of PERSON A (R. Ramesh Kumar / Ramesh Kumar / R. Kumar / Kumar, Ramesh / Ramesh Kumar R.) resolved to ONE primary subject?
MERGE_test.pass: Primary subject = R. Ramesh Kumar (or an equivalent single identity); the variant forms are recognised as the same person, not scattered as separate entities or false conflicts.
MERGE_test.fail: The subject is fragmented into multiple people, OR a variant form is picked as a separate associate.

SPLIT_test_CRITICAL.check: Is PERSON B (S. Kumar Ramesh / Kumar Ramesh) kept SEPARATE from the subject?
SPLIT_test_CRITICAL.pass: S. Kumar Ramesh appears as a DISTINCT associate, never merged into the subject.
SPLIT_test_CRITICAL.fail: S. Kumar Ramesh is merged into R. Ramesh Kumar (token-order / shared-token false merge). THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT CHECK.

initial_collision_test.check: Is PERSON E (R. Suresh) kept separate from the subject (R. Ramesh Kumar)?
initial_collision_test.pass: R. Suresh is a distinct associate.
initial_collision_test.fail: R. Suresh merged with the subject on the shared 'R.' initial.

distinct_associates_test.check: Do §05/§08 associations list PERSON B, C, D, E as distinct named associates?
distinct_associates_test.pass: All four distinct associates appear separately with citations.

benami_attribution_test.check: Are the accounts/entities held under the subject's variant names (Ramesh Kumar R., R. Kumar, Kumar Ramesh) attributed to the SUBJECT, while S. Kumar Ramesh's Dubai wire stays with ASSOCIATE B?
benami_attribution_test.pass: Subject's fragmented holdings consolidate to him; associate's holdings stay separate.

junk_seeded_for_regression.doubled_name_row: R. Ramesh Kumar R. Ramesh Kumar

also_exercises_pattern_engine: LAYERING_STRUCTURE (kickback in → shell transfers → cross-border wire)
NETWORK_HUB (subject central to associates and shells)
expected_challenges_summary: The single hardest check is SPLIT_test_CRITICAL: keeping 'S. Kumar Ramesh' distinct from 'R. Ramesh Kumar'. A weak resolver merges them because they share both tokens. A strong resolver notices the reversed order + different initial + distinct phone/account and keeps them separate. Second-hardest: MERGE_test — pulling the subject's 5 scattered name-forms into one person without help.
all_fictional: All persons, entities, numbers, accounts, tenders, and case references fictional. Investigation file only. The naming complexity is a deliberate stress test of entity resolution.
